subject: Region sequestration and grace-period Q&A for Dedicated tenancy
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@clariohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@clariohealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on region sequestration + deletion grace periods (Dedicated)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — ClarioHealth is excited about Redwood Dedicated. Before we move to the legal draft, procurement has a few technical clarifications we need written down for our security team regarding region "sequestration" and deletion behavior: 

- If we pin a Dedicated pool to an in-country region, can you confirm whether any snapshots/backups of that pool are ever replicated outside the pinned region?
- Is there a configurable retention/grace period for deletions (e.g., user/tenant wipe) where data is soft-deleted before irreversible purge? If so, what is the default and the maximum we can set?
- For restore/recovery operations after a wipe, do any of those flows temporarily move data to a control-plane region outside our pinned region (even transiently)?
- What evidence/artifacts can Redwood provide to show an erase operation completed (logs, wipe tickets, snapshot deletion timestamps)?

We would like this in writing to attach to our vendor review packet. Happy to hop on a 30m call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Senior InfoSec Manager, ClarioHealth
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@clariohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on region sequestration + deletion grace periods (Dedicated)

Maria —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a data flow map and our wipe playbook for your packet. If your legal team needs more formal wording we can produce an attestation.

1) Snapshots/backups: For Dedicated pools pinned to a specific region, we do not replicate persistent snapshots or backups outside the pinned region by default. We retain a single-regional snapshot replication topology for recovery. Cross-region replication is only enabled by explicit customer request and is subject to contract amendment.

2) Deletion grace period: There are two layers:
  - Tenant-level soft-delete: when a tenant is marked for deletion we have a configurable soft-delete window (default 14 days). During this period data is retained but inaccessible to the tenant.
  - Irreversible purge: after the soft-delete window, background purge jobs run and artifacts (live data, KV cache, and associated snapshots) are removed and overwritten per our wipe playbook. The soft-delete window can be configured from 0–90 days per customer policy.

3) Control-plane/transient flows: The control plane coordinates operations from our management region, but data paths for active Dedicated pools remain in-region. Any control-plane metadata (operation ids, job status, timestamps) may be stored outside the tenancy region for operational auditability, but not customer data or readable snapshots. If a restore requires pulling a snapshot, that snapshot is read from the pinned region only.

4) Evidence/artifacts: We can provide:
  - Wipe ticket with job id and timestamps
  - Snapshot deletion logs including object ids and deletion timestamps
  - Audit trail entries (operation id, user/service actor, IP ranges)
  - Optional signed attestation (PDF) on completion

Attachments: data_flow_map.pdf (diagram), redwood-dedicated-wipe-playbook-v1.docx (procedure).

Next steps: I can coordinate a short call between you, Ben (ops), and Kimberly (legal) to convert this into contractual language. Do mornings on Monday look good for you?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@clariohealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on region sequestration + deletion grace periods (Dedicated)

Maria — quick follow from ops/legal perspective:

- Replication topology: confirmed — persistent snapshots and storage objects for a pinned Dedicated pool are created and deleted in-region unless you request cross-region replication in the order. We can add a clause that cross-region replication requires written consent and a scoping call.

- Soft-delete/purge mechanics: soft-delete is implemented via metadata flag and retention TTL. Purge jobs are idempotent and will attempt deletion until object store confirms removal. We will provide a deletion manifest (list of object ids) and S3-compatible deletion confirmation logs.

- Backup lifecycle: ephemeral cache snapshots (KV cache) are kept only for warm-starts and are considered volatile — they are zeroed on tenant wipe; persistent model artifacts are not part of tenant data.

- Transient reads: restores operate within pinned region. Control-plane only holds operation metadata and no PII or model input/output artifacts.

I can provide a short, contract-ready paragraph for your data-residency annex. Kimberly — can you draft the attestation language and sign-off flow?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what our security team needs. A couple of small asks before we close the vendor review: 

- Can Redwood provide the deletion manifest and snapshot deletion logs as a redacted sample we can attach to our packet?
- We'd like the soft-delete window to be configurable to 30 days for our default; please confirm that goes into the order form/annex.
- If you can draft the attestation paragraph, we'll circulate to Contracts and request a DocuSign signature.

We'll plan a 30m exec-level call Monday 10:00–10:30 PT to finalize annex language. Please include Kimberly on the call invite.

Best,
Maria
Senior InfoSec Manager, ClarioHealth
